description.narrative:
Programmet syftar till att främja hälsa, rättigheter och välbefinnande för alla människor, särskilt kvinnor, ungdomar och unga. UNFPA:s mål i Tanzania är i linje med dess globala mandat att stödja uppnåendet av universell tillgång till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR), minska mödradödlighet och säkerställa kvinnors och ungas egenmakt.
De huvudsakliga målen är:
Att förbättra tillgången till kvalitativa tjänster inom sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa. Att främja ungdomars och ungas egenmakt. Att motverka könsbaserat våld (GBV) och skadliga sedvänjor. Att stärka befolkningsdata och policyutveckling. Att bygga motståndskraft i humanitära sammanhang. UNFPA:s arbete i Tanzania är anpassat till landets utvecklingsvision 2025 samt till de globala hållbarhetsmålen (SDG), särskilt målen som rör hälsa, jämställdhet och minskade ojämlikheter.

The Program aims to promote the health, rights, and well-being of all people, particularly women, adolescents, and youth. The objectives of UNFPA in Tanzania align with its global mandate to support the achievement of universal access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), reduce maternal mortality, and ensure the empowerment of women and young people. The main objectives are Improving Access to Quality Sexual and Reproductive Health Services, Promoting Adolescent and Youth Empowerment, Addressing Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and Harmful Practices, Strengthening Population Data and Policy and Building Resilience in Humanitarian Settings. The work of UNFPA in Tanzania is aligned with the country’s Development Vision 2025, as well as the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly goals related to health, gender equality, and reducing inequalities.

The objective of the intervention outlined in the UNFPA's 9th Country Programme for Tanzania is to achieve universal access to sexual and reproductive health and the realization of reproductive rights. Specifically, by the end of the intervention, the programme aims to:
Reduce the unmet need for family planning.Decrease preventable maternal deaths.Curb gender-based violence and harmful practices, such as female genital mutilation and child marriage.
These goals align with the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and contribute to achieving Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDGs 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and SDG 5 (Gender Equality).

description.narrative:
Results from the 2025 Annual Report:
Expanded access to family planning: UNFPA Tanzania has procured and distributed essential reproductive health commodities, contributing to an estimated 516 maternal deaths, 172,075 unintended pregnancies, and 2,409 child deaths averted. The support has also provided more than 3.5 million people with access to modern family planning services, including nearly 2 million women in UNFPA-supported regions.
Strengthened maternal and newborn health systems: UNFPA Tanzania has developed the Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR) digital notification platform in Zanzibar, enabling real-time monitoring of maternal and perinatal deaths and improving evidence-based decision-making. Health worker training has also contributed to declining maternal mortality trends in several supported regions.
Improved quality of SRHR services: UNFPA Tanzania has trained 339 health care workers in emergency obstetric and newborn care, maternal death surveillance, family planning/HIV integration, and labour care. Supported regions reported over 3.15 million family planning clients and 3.54 million HIV tests.
Empowered adolescents and young people: UNFPA Tanzania has reached 20,000 students in higher learning institutions on mainland Tanzania and 2,078 young people in Zanzibar with SRHR, HIV and GBV information. More than 300 youth were linked to youth-friendly health facilities for HIV testing and contraceptive services. Through digital platforms, over 463,000 adolescents, young people and caregivers accessed SRHR information.
Economic empowerment of young women and persons with disabilities: UNFPA Tanzania has supported 250 first-time young mothers with entrepreneurship, financial literacy and SRHR training, while equipping the Yombo Vocational Training Centre with tools and equipment benefiting 260 young people with disabilities and strengthening livelihood opportunities.
Strengthened policies and inclusion: UNFPA Tanzania has supported the development of the 20262030 Strategic Plan for the Zanzibar National Council for Persons with Disabilities and the revision of the Zanzibar HIV Policy, improving protection of the rights of persons with disabilities and strengthening the policy framework for inclusive SRHR services.
Enhanced national data systems: UNPFA Tanzania has supported studies on the links between climate change and SRHR, strengthened civil registration and vital statistics (CRVS) systems in Zanzibar, and promoted the use of data for evidence-based planning through the Zanzibar Statistical Forum.
